title: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities & Contingent Assets (Dispute Probability Triangulation & Footnote Disclosures)

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Continuous legal status review, assessment of probability shifts, and provision discounting review at reporting dates

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 37 (converged with IAS 37 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 450), entities must distinguish between Provisions, Contingent Liabilities, and Contingent Assets. A Provision is recognized if and only if: (1) an entity has a present legal or constructive obligation as a result of a past event; (2) it is probable (more likely than not, i.e. > 50% probability) that an outflow of economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation; and (3) a reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation. Provisions are recognized as balance sheet liabilities and expensed in the Statement of Profit and Loss (discounted to present value where the time value of money is material). A Contingent Liability is a possible obligation whose existence will be confirmed only by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain future events not wholly within the control of the entity (typically 5% to 50% probability), or a present obligation that is not recognized because an outflow is not probable or cannot be reliably measured. Contingent liabilities are never recognized on the balance sheet; instead, they are disclosed in Schedule III Notes to Accounts with estimates of financial effect and uncertainties. If the probability of outflow is Remote (< 5%), neither recognition nor disclosure is required. A Contingent Asset is never recognized in financial statements unless realization is virtually certain; it is disclosed only when an inflow of economic benefits is probable. For corporate statutory defense, tax demands (disputed GST notices under Sections 73/74, disputed Income Tax assessment additions under appeal before CIT(A) or ITAT, and customs disputes) must be rigorously evaluated against this probability matrix to prevent both premature balance sheet over-accruals and audit qualification for non-disclosure.
